findings.failure_path: When python3 is missing or host-input.py is unreadable, any non-apply_patch tool (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit) only gets a systemMessage and is allowed. Before this change, jq read file_path and enforced .worktree-only and live-worktree denial with no Python. Primary-checkout edits on Claude now go through.
findings.smallest_fix: When Python is unavailable and the tool is not apply_patch, keep the old jq extraction (.tool_input.file_path // notebook_path // path) and run check_target on that path. Add an isolated-hooks test that expects Edit into the protected repo to be denied.

findings.failure_path: The apply_patch loop exits on the first non-empty response. With strict:false, the first target gets an advisory additionalContext (an ask converted to advisory), the loop prints it and exits 0, and later targets are never checked. A later deny, for example from a missing or expired boundary, never fires, so a deny can lose to an advisory.
findings.smallest_fix: Collect every target's response. Output the first permissionDecision deny if there is one; otherwise output the advisory. Add a test with an advisory first target and a deny second target.

findings.failure_path: prior_handoff becomes true after any earlier non-fenced assistant proposed-next line anywhere in the transcript, and it stays true. Every later unrelated final answer, such as a question or a 'Stopped as requested.' reply (which the tests expect to be blocked), then gets a forced continuation. That pushes the model past a user stop into writing a next-action line.
findings.smallest_fix: Treat a prior handoff as eligible only if it is in the latest assistant final before the current user turn. Leave the final unblocked when it answers a stop or status-only request.

findings.failure_path: transcript_lines silently stops after 20,000 events or 16 MB, and after any single line over 1 MB. In long sessions, apply_patch or Edit events past that point never reach edit_paths, so skill-extraction-gate-stop exits 0 without blocking. The output does not signal the truncation, so the gate cannot tell a partial scan from a full one.
findings.smallest_fix: Return a truncated flag, or scan the tail instead of the head. Have the Stop gates emit an 'unverified' systemMessage when the scan was truncated.

concern_results.conclusion: Found three problems. (1) If Python is missing, Claude Edit/Write isolation now fails open; before this change, jq alone enforced it. (2) In owner-dispatch, an advisory result for an earlier patch target ends the loop, so a deny for a later target never runs. (3) One earlier proposed-next line makes every later Stop eligible for a reminder. Scanning a long transcript also stops at 20,000 events or 16 MB, and edits after that point are missed. Repeated Stop loops are blocked by the strict stop_hook_active === false check.
The tests miss both bypasses. The missing-normalizer test only checks apply_patch, not Edit. No test mixes an advisory target with a later deny target.

challenge_focus: Attack fail-open isolation without Python, all-target deny precedence, proposed-next false eligibility and repeated Stop loops, malformed transcript and context budgets. Authorization scripts and package inventory have separate partition receipts; assess only runtime packet, not missing unrelated partitions.
